title: Impact of the Middle East war on UK living standards
subject: What energy, motor fuel and food price rises from the Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption would cost UK households in 2027-28 under three annual stress-test scenarios (cost per household, the energy channel and people newly below an anchored poverty line), and the gross cost of ten policy responses.
search_terms: Middle East war UK living standards
Strait of Hormuz energy prices households
oil price shock UK households cost
energy price shock poverty UK households

epg.description: The analysis's stylised Energy Price Guarantee: government pays each household's energy bill rise above 10% of its baseline energy spending (EPG_CAP_PCT = 0.10), for 2027-28.

flat_rebate.description: A flat £400 energy rebate to every household in 2027-28, modelled on the 2022 Energy Bills Support Scheme.

ct_rebate.description: A £300 rebate to every household in council tax bands A to D, UK-wide (stylised; the 2022 scheme paid £150 in England).

uc_uplift.description: A £20 a week uplift to every Universal Credit recipient household for 2027-28, matching the 2020-21 uplift.

fuel_duty_cut.description: A 5p a litre fuel duty cut for the whole of 2027-28, after the cut in force to 31 December 2026. The pinned outlay is 5p on each vehicle-owning household's modelled petrol and diesel litres (compute_policies); a separate PolicyEngine reform cutting PolicyEngine's 2027-28 rate of 59.25p by 5p gives the same £2.18bn (parameters.fuel_duty_exchequer_cost).

means_tested.description: A £650 cost-of-living payment in two instalments (£326 and £324) to households on a benefit that qualified for the 2022 payment, each paid at an assumed 85% per-window entitlement rate.

elec_vat_cut.description: VAT on domestic electricity at 0% rather than 5% for the whole of 2027-28, extending the cut in force from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027, for every UK household: compute_policies applies it with no region filter, so Northern Ireland is included, while the enacted cut covers Great Britain only.

accelerated_uprating.description: CPI-uprated benefit rates raised at once by each scenario's residual CPI addition (the part of the shock September 2026 CPI did not capture), for 2027-28.

social_tariff.description: Households on Universal Credit or with household net income below £20,000 have half of their energy price rise offset.

combined.description: The eight measures other than the social tariff applied together, the Energy Price Guarantee capping the bill before the electricity VAT relief applies to it.

elec_vat_cut_six_months.description: The enacted temporary zero rate of VAT on domestic electricity in Great Britain from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027 (announced 21 July 2026).

elec_vat_cut_gb_continued.description: The Great Britain zero rate of VAT on domestic electricity continued after 31 March 2027: IFS's 'permanent' cut, and RF's annual cost of the cut in future years.

fuel_duty_gradual_reversal.description: Resolution Foundation: small quarterly fuel duty rises that reverse the 5p cut and then raise duty by, say, 3 per cent a year, costed against current policy.

uc_and_pension_credit_uprating_brought_f.description: Resolution Foundation: the Parliament's planned above-inflation rises in the Universal Credit standard allowance brought forward to September 2026, with an equivalent temporary boost for Pension Credit.

fuel_duty_5p_permanent_and_freeze.description: IFS Green Budget 2026: the 5p fuel duty cut made permanent and fuel duty rates frozen for a further year instead of rising with RPI.

fuel_duty_freeze_to_2030.description: IFS Green Budget 2026: the 5p fuel duty cut made permanent and the freeze extended until 2029-30.

epg_style_cap_at_april_2026.description: JRF: an Energy Price Guarantee-style intervention capping energy prices at the April 2026 Ofgem price cap, on July 2026 cost projections.

energy_discounts_offset_cpi_rise.description: Resolution Foundation: energy price discounts large enough to offset the roughly 1.5 percentage point rise in the Bank of England's inflation outlook for Q3 2026, continued for a year.

uc_uplift_10_six_months.description: NIESR: a temporary £10 a week uplift to Universal Credit for six months over the autumn and winter.

tuc_standard_social_tariff.description: TUC: a 25% bill reduction for households below the relative poverty line and 15% for those between it and median income (equivalised BHC household income).

tuc_energy_crisis_social_tariff.description: TUC: during an energy crisis, a 30%, 20% or 10% bill reduction for households below the relative poverty line, below median income and below mean income respectively.
